requirements.text: The THEMAS system shall control the heating and cooling units that are defined as part of the THEMAS system.
The system shall read this file and the definitions shall be derived from the initialization data in the file.
The THEMAS system shall use the information contained in the initialization data file to determine which heating and cooling units are part of the THEMAS system.
Each thermostat shall have a unique identifier by which that thermostat is identified in the THEMAS system.
The initialization file shall contain a unique identifier for each thermostat that the system is to monitor.
These identifiers shall be read from the initialization file and loaded into the THEMAS system during the initialization process.
There shall be a maximum number of heating or cooling u nits that can be on at any given time.
The maximum number of concurrently running units shall be read from the initialization file and stored in the THEMAS system.
This procedure shall read the initialization file and establish the trigger value from the data in that file.
The THEMAS system shall en sure the temperature reported by a given thermostat shall not exceed a maximum deviation value of 3 degrees Fahrenheit.
This procedure shall read the initialization file and establish the overtemperature value from the data in that file.
The THEMAS system shall onl y respond to temperatures that are within a reasonable value.
This procedure shall read the initialization file and establish the valid temperature range from the data in it.
When the THEMAS system is initialized, it shall first turn off all the heating and cooling units.
The THEMAS system shall only respond to temperatures from the thermostats that are within the specified valid range.
The THEMAS system shall determine wh en a reported temperature or a changed temperature setting exceeds the limits set by the overtemperature values.
When the current temperature value exceeds the current temperature setting by a pre -defined amount, the THEMAS system shall activate the appropriate heating or cooling unit.
The THEMAS system shall limit the number of heating or cooling units t hat may be running simultaneously.
When a request for a heating unit or cooling to be turned is denied, an event shall be generated and the THEMAS system shall record that event.
The THEMAS system shall control the heating and cooling units that are designated as part of the THEMAS system.
Once a request to turn on or off a heating or cooling unit, the THEMAS system shall provide the necessary control signal for the unit.
For each event that is generated, the THEMAS system shall identify each event and generate the appropriate event data.
The THEMAS system shall provide the supervisor a mechanism to change the temperature setting of any of the thermostats in the system.

The THEMAS shall provide the ability for the supervisor to select between two different types of reports: 1) the operational history of the THEMAS system for the past twelve months and 2) a statistical summary for any selected mont h.
The THEMAS system shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) requiring authentication for any supervisor-level actions, including changing thermostat settings or generating reports.
The system shall verify the integrity of the initialization file before loading, and access to the file shall be restricted to authorized system processes.
The event database shall be protected with access controls, and sensitive event data shall be stored in a secure, encrypted format to prevent unauthorized modification or viewing.
The THEMAS system shall define a valid temperature range of -20°F to 130°F; any input outside this range shall be flagged as an error.
The THEMAS system shall detect a loss of communication with any thermostat within 5 seconds and trigger a 'Communication Failure' alarm.
The THEMAS system shall interface with H/C units via a standard Modbus TCP protocol or equivalent documented API.
The H/C request queue shall have a maximum capacity of 100 requests; if exceeded, the oldest request shall be dropped and an error logged.
The THEMAS system shall generate the 12-month operational history report within 60 seconds of user request.
The system shall process temperature data and issue the corresponding heating/cooling control signal within 500 milliseconds of receiving the temperature input.
The system shall support a minimum of 12 thermostats and 12 heating/cooling units as described in the building layout.
The system shall generate an operational history report for a 12-month period within 30 seconds of the request.
The system shall be capable of storing at least 100,000 events per month in the database without performance degradation.
